QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_48

question.text: If a trader fails to deliver shares under physical settlement of stock derivatives, the clearing corporation:

answer.text: Conducts a buy-in auction to procure the shares and charges the defaulting member a penalty
Converts the position to cash settlement without penalty
Extends the delivery deadline by one week
Cancels the trade as if it never happened

explanation.text: The Logic: Non-fulfilment of a securities deliverable obligation under physical settlement is treated as a settlement violation. In general clearing-corporation practice, the corporation invokes a close-out / buy-in mechanism — procuring the undelivered shares so the buyer receives them — and recovers the cost from the defaulting member, alongside penalties and possible disciplinary action. The settlement guarantee is preserved; the cost falls on the defaulter, not the counterparty. The Trap: The trade is not cancelled as if it never happened, the obligation is not silently converted to cash settlement without consequence, and deadlines are not extended at will. Each of those would undermine settlement-guarantee discipline. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (156, 170-171) describe physical-delivery procedures and list non-fulfilment of securities deliverable obligation as a violation attracting penalties and disciplinary action, but the explicit term "buy-in auction" and that specific procurement procedure were not located in the pages checked. The framing above reflects general clearing-corporation practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
